from datetime import timedelta
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.utils.dates import days_ago

default_args = {
    "retries": 3,
    "retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=2),
    "retry_exponential_backoff": True,
    "max_retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=20),
}

with DAG("nightly_ingest", schedule_interval="0 2 * * *", start_date=days_ago(1),
         catchup=False, default_args=default_args, max_active_runs=1) as nightly_ingest:
    pass  # sensors >> ingest >> transform >> quality gate >> publish

def pull_partner_drop(partner, ds, dest):
    """Wait for <file>.done, compare the size with manifest.json, then copy to the landing path."""
    manifest = json.loads(read_remote(partner, f"{ds}/manifest.json"))
    for name, size in manifest["files"].items():
        copy_verified(partner, f"{ds}/{name}", dest, size)

-- grain: one row per order_id per ds; unique key: order_id
INSERT INTO fact_orders
SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.amount * fx.rate AS amount_usd, o.ds
FROM staging.orders o
JOIN fx_rates fx ON fx.currency = o.currency AND fx.rate_date = o.rate_date
WHERE o.ds = '{{ ds }}';

def export_parquet(df, dest, row_group_mb=128):
    df.write.option("parquet.block.size", row_group_mb * 1024 * 1024) \
      .config("spark.sql.parquet.outputTimestampType", "TIMESTAMP_MICROS") \
      .parquet(dest)

fields.rule: never write raw email, phone or national id values to logs, task output or warehouse error tables; mask with pii.masking first
fields.exceptions: the vault table, which is access controlled

fields.rule: every task must be safe to re-run for the same ds: replace the partition, never append to it
fields.enforced_by: review and the rerun test in CI

fields.title: Pull partner SFTP drops only after the .done marker and a manifest size match
fields.context: Acme uploads large files in place; INC-318 loaded a half written 4 GB file as if it were complete, so the pull task must handle a file that is still being written and now compares each size with manifest.json before copying

fields.description: Acme's Sunday drop lands between 03:10 and 06:40 UTC, not at midnight, so the SFTP sensor has to wait up to 4 hours in reschedule mode before it fails

fields.name: offset_pagination_skip
fields.signature: paging the Bravo orders API by offset while new orders arrive skips or repeats rows; nightly counts drifted by about 0.3 percent

fields.fix_template: follow the next_cursor token and save it in the ingest state after every page so a retry resumes where it stopped
fields.caveats: a cursor expires after 15 minutes; on a 410 restart from the stored high water mark

fields.constraint: at most 5 requests a second per token; on a 429 sleep for Retry-After and do not open parallel pages
fields.reason: INC-331: three parallel pagers got our token blocked for 6 hours

fields.name: unbounded_http_wait
fields.signature: an HTTP call without a read timeout idles on a stalled socket until the task's execution_timeout kills it

fields.title: Ingest task hung for 9 hours on a stalled REST page
fields.root_cause: the page request had no read timeout and the partner's load balancer kept the connection open (INC-342)

fields.title: Fetch partner SFTP keys from the secrets backend at the start of each attempt
fields.context: keys pasted into the Airflow connection UI were rotated by hand and broke the 02:00 run (INC-305); fetching by secret name means a rotation needs no deploy

fields.purpose: pulls partner drops, verifies the manifest and lands raw files, one task per partner

fields.title: Retry every task 3 times with exponential backoff capped at 20 minutes
fields.context: a flat 5 minute retry kept hammering the warehouse during the INC-297 outage and the retrying tasks held their queue slots

fields.constraint: pool warehouse_load has 6 slots; do not raise it above 8
fields.reason: past 8 concurrent COPY statements the warehouse queues them and p95 load time doubles

fields.description: a newly deployed DAG with catchup=True schedules every missed ds since its start_date at once; leave catchup False and use the backfill DAG for history

fields.title: Schedule each DAG in the partner's local time zone
fields.context: partners think in their own business day, so a 02:00 local schedule lines up with their drop

fields.title: Schedule every DAG in UTC
fields.context: the March daylight saving change ran the nightly job twice for one logical date (INC-288) under the Europe/Berlin schedule; UTC has no repeated hour

fields.pattern: every DAG file must import cleanly in the DagBag test with no network and no credentials; the test fails on any import error

fields.name: dag_parse_cost
fields.signature: API calls or warehouse queries at module level in a DAG file run on every scheduler parse and stretched the parse loop to 4 minutes

fields.fix_template: move the lookup into a task callable or a Variable read inside a template, so parsing a DAG file does no I/O
fields.caveats: template rendering happens at run time, so a bad value shows up as a task failure rather than an import error

fields.title: Run Spark tasks on the spark queue and light SQL tasks on the default queue
fields.context: a Spark job holding a worker slot for 50 minutes starved the quality checks behind it (INC-311)

fields.description: each Celery worker process grows by about 40 MB per task after importing pandas, so workers are recycled after 20 tasks with max_tasks_per_child

fields.name: orders_partition_merge
fields.frequency: every night for 18 partitions, about 40 minutes of the 3 hour batch window

fields.question: Should nightly_ingest split into one DAG per partner so a late drop from one partner does not hold the whole queue?

fields.decision: migrate task logs to remote storage on S3 before the Airflow upgrade
fields.rationale: local worker disks reached 85 percent from 14 days of task logs (OPS-71)

fields.rule: write one JSON log line per task with dag_id, task_id, ds and row_count; no print statements

fields.title: Set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to 400 for the sessionize job
fields.context: the default 200 gave 2 GB shuffle partitions and executors died with OOM (INC-322); 400 brings each to about 600 MB

fields.name: hot_key_skew
fields.signature: a null or default customer_id sends 30 percent of events to one reducer and the sessionize stage runs for 3 hours

fields.fix_template: drop null customer_id rows first and salt the remaining hot keys into 16 buckets before the window, then merge the buckets
fields.caveats: remove the salt column before writing; a session that spans two buckets must be re-joined

fields.preferred_form: row_number() over (partition by event_id order by ingested_at desc) = 1 in a QUALIFY clause
fields.avoid: SELECT DISTINCT, which keeps both copies when a late row differs in a single column

fields.rule: each transform file opens with a comment naming its grain and unique key; the test runner asserts that key is unique after every build

fields.cases_required: running the same ds twice gives identical row counts, a late arriving row updates in place, an empty partition writes zero rows without an error

fields.option: Rewrite the SQL transforms in dbt
fields.rejected_because: the Spark sessionization steps and the lineage emitter would have had to stay outside it, and the migration was estimated at 6 weeks with no change in output

fields.description: fx rates are published for weekdays only, so Saturday and Sunday orders must take Friday's rate; joining on the exact date silently drops about 9 percent of weekend revenue

fields.name: float_money
fields.signature: amounts cast to double in a Spark step drift from the finance ledger by cents after summing

fields.title: Revenue totals drifted a few cents from finance
fields.root_cause: the sessionize join cast amount to double; DECIMAL(18,4) end to end fixed it (INC-300)

fields.depth: deep: took the job from 90 minutes to 25

fields.approach: rewrite sessionize as pure SQL window functions
fields.reason_failed: the gap window scanned 3 days of events per partition and cost 4 times the Spark job

fields.description: cannot upgrade Spark to 3.5 until the cluster vendor ships the Iceberg connector fix (VEN-12)

records.retracted: reproduced with adaptive execution on after the skew fix, so it was never the cause

fields.name: aqe_regression
fields.signature: adaptive query execution coalesces sessionize partitions too far and the stage runs slower

fields.title: Load by replacing the whole ds partition instead of row level MERGE
fields.context: MERGE on the 1.2 billion row fact took 55 minutes and could not handle a rerun after a partial failure; delete then insert inside one transaction is atomic

fields.rule: migrate a warehouse table by building <name>_v2, backfilling it, then renaming both in one transaction; never ALTER a column type in place

fields.constraint: cluster key is (ds, customer_id) and every query must filter on ds
fields.reason: an unfiltered scan reads 11 TB, takes 20 minutes and blocks the metrics API connection pool

fields.name: small_file_explosion
fields.signature: backfills that write one tiny parquet file per task produced 380,000 objects and list calls took minutes

fields.fix_template: compact each partition to 256 MB files in a compact task right after the load
fields.caveats: run it before the quality gate, otherwise row counts read a stale file list

fields.title: Keep raw landing files for 90 days and fact tables for 7 years
fields.context: the finance audit needs seven years of orders, while raw files older than 90 days can be re-fetched from the partner

fields.description: COPY INTO silently truncates strings longer than the column unless ON_ERROR is set to ABORT; INC-327 lost the tail of 14,000 product names before anyone noticed

fields.purpose: loads staged parquet into fact tables one ds partition at a time and records row counts

fields.description: customer_region is free text and has 41 spellings of EMEA; it should be an enum with a lookup table

fields.title: Dimension tables grew to 3 times their size
fields.root_cause: dead rows were never vacuumed because the metrics API pool holds a snapshot open for hours (OPS-77)

fields.solution: run VACUUM on the dimension tables by hand every Monday.
fields.description: the automatic vacuum skips tables with open readers, until the metrics pool recycles its connections (OPS-77)

fields.title: Keep partner schemas as JSON files in the repo with no registry
fields.context: simple, reviewable in a pull request and no extra service to run

fields.title: Run a schema registry as the source of truth for data contracts
fields.context: the JSON files in the repo drifted from what partners really sent and nobody noticed until INC-270

fields.title: Enforce BACKWARD compatibility on every registry subject
fields.context: a partner dropping the currency column broke fact_orders at 03:00 (INC-295); the registry now rejects removed columns and type narrowing

fields.description: Acme adds optional columns without notice about once a quarter, so the import must ignore unknown columns and emit a schema_drift warning instead of failing the task

fields.name: silent_null_cast
fields.signature: a partner changed a column from int to string and the reader turned the unparsable values into null, which then passed as zero

fields.fix_template: read partner files with the contract schema in FAILFAST mode so a bad cast fails the task
fields.caveats: route the failure to quarantine rather than retrying, since a retry cannot fix bad data

fields.title: Fail the quality gate when a partition has under 70 percent of the 7 day median row count
fields.context: an empty partner file loaded zero rows and passed every not-null check (INC-314)

fields.rule: checks tagged severity=error block publish and severity=warn only open a ticket; a new check starts as warn for two weeks

fields.pattern: unit test each check against a tiny parquet fixture with one passing and one failing partition; tests never run checks against the real warehouse

fields.title: Freshness check failed every Monday
fields.root_cause: it compared max(ingested_at) with now and ignored that the Sunday drop lands at 06:40 UTC (INC-336)

fields.decision: move check thresholds out of Python into quality/expectations.yaml
fields.rationale: analysts can review a threshold change in a pull request without reading the check runner

fields.name: quarantine_partition
fields.template: a failed partition is moved to quarantine.<table>_<ds> and the publish task is skipped rather than failed
fields.usage_context: any blocking quality failure; downstream DAGs read only published tables

records.retracted: found null customer_ids produced by our own left join as well

fields.description: null customer_id values come only from the web partner's feed, so ignore them for the other partners

fields.title: Backfill by truncating and reloading the whole table
fields.context: the simplest way to guarantee no stale rows are left behind

fields.title: Backfill in 7 day chunks with max_active_runs of 2
fields.context: a 400 day backfill started as 400 parallel runs, filled the warehouse queue and delayed the nightly load by 5 hours (INC-320)

fields.rule: announce each backfill with the table, ds range and expected cost before starting, and set backfill=true in the run conf so alerts stay muted

fields.state: weeks 1 to 9 done; week 10 failed on a missing fx rate, resume from 2025-03-05

fields.title: A backfill cost 4,200 dollars in one night
fields.root_cause: the backfill DAG ran under a service account on the budget guard's exempt list (INC-339)

fields.title: Block queries whose dry run estimate is over 500 GB scanned unless they carry an approval tag
fields.context: an unfiltered scan cost 55 dollars (INC-309); the guard calls a dry run before it submits anything

fields.constraint: at most 40 executors, spot instances everywhere except the publish stage
fields.reason: monthly compute rose from 18k to 31k dollars after autoscaling was left unbounded in September

fields.title: Cache metric responses for 60 seconds keyed by query hash and ds range
fields.context: the wall dashboards update every 10 seconds on 30 screens and hit the warehouse 180 times a minute

fields.constraint: p95 under 800 ms and at most 50,000 points per response
fields.reason: the BI tool times out at 1 second and retries, which doubles the load

fields.rule: error responses use the problem+json shape with a trace_id; never return a stack trace or SQL text to a caller

fields.name: gold table read model
fields.why_chosen: the API only reads pre-aggregated gold tables, so latency does not depend on fact table size

records.retracted: the stale values came from one worker with a skewed clock, not from the cache

fields.title: Metrics API served yesterday's numbers after publish
fields.root_cause: the 60 second cache key ignored the publish version

fields.title: Run analyst notebooks through the notebook runner in a sandbox pod with a 30 minute limit
fields.context: a notebook left its Spark session open over a weekend and cost 900 dollars (INC-317)

fields.rule: strip outputs before commit, document the inputs in the first cell, and write results only to the analytics_sandbox schema; notebooks never write to gold tables

fields.pattern: smoke test every scheduled notebook with the runner in dry-run mode against the sample dataset; the whole test run must stay under 2 minutes

records.retracted: memory growth was the open Spark session, not pandas

fields.name: kernel_memory_leak
fields.signature: long notebook runs grow to 12 GB because pandas never releases intermediate frames

fields.title: Offer Parquet as the default export and CSV only up to 1 million rows
fields.context: customers' 40 million row CSV exports timed out and the Parquet file is 8 times smaller (SUP-902)

fields.name: parquet_int96_timestamps
fields.signature: Spark wrote timestamps as INT96 and a customer's reader showed them as 1970 dates

fields.fix_template: set spark.sql.parquet.outputTimestampType to TIMESTAMP_MICROS in the export's Spark config
fields.caveats: exports written before the change must be regenerated, so tell the customer

fields.constraint: stream in 128 MB row groups and keep driver memory under 4 GB; never collect() a result
fields.reason: INC-306: collect() on the orders export killed the driver at 9 GB

fields.rule: customer facing exports pass through pii.masking with the export's column allowlist; a column that is not on the list is dropped, not exported

fields.title: Tokenize email and phone with a keyed HMAC in staging and keep raw values only in the vault table
fields.context: a GDPR erasure (GDPR-88) then touches one table instead of 60

fields.template: delete the vault row, null the token column in staging and rerun the affected ds partitions through the transform
fields.usage_context: a GDPR erasure ticket; the whole process must finish within 30 days and write the audit table entry

fields.title: Email addresses found in Airflow task logs
fields.root_cause: a debug log of the REST response body wrote customer emails (INC-325)

fields.description: one global HMAC key; quarterly rotation needs a key version column that does not exist yet

fields.title: Read config from per environment YAML overlays and secrets only from the secrets backend
fields.context: a staging bucket name committed in settings.py pointed production exports at staging (INC-310)

fields.rule: every new config key needs a default in settings.py and a line in the config reference document; deploy refuses unknown keys

fields.name: with_retry
fields.usage_context: any call to a partner API or the warehouse; never retry on a validation error

fields.title: Sync DAG files to the scheduler bucket only after the DagBag test passes
fields.context: a syntax error pushed at 01:50 stopped the whole nightly run (INC-289)
